newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian MTBE - Weak gasoline starting to haunt market.
newsitem.headline: Asian MTBE - Weak gasoline starting to haunt market.

text.p: Asia's weak gasoline prices returned this week to haunt MTBE sellers and could keep a lid on the octane booster near term.
"I am optimistic on the U.S gas gasoline demand as it moves to high gear with the summer driving season but demand in the east is not very inspiring," said a seller with a western firm.
"The market here is shaky but as long as the U.S. offers an alternative to prevent the market from plunging, prices may find some support somewhere," he added.
Traders said various tender news might offer some support for the market, but worries about gasoline prices would temper the upside.
One trader said the arbitrage to the U.S. Gulf from the Far East is wide opened, allowing surplus supplies to flow west if weak demand in Asia persisted.
Singapore free-on-board (fob) MTBE prices for July were assessed unchanged this week from last week at $255/$260 per tonne, sources said.
Gasoline prices in Singapore were lower this week, undermined as major oil companies looked to offload surplus stocks. Demand has been poor.
Benchmark 95-octant gasoline was last assessed at $23.95 a barrel fob Singapore, down 40 cents from the same point last week.
A Singapore trader said MTBE prices for most of July were expected to be stable in the absence of factors to push prices one way or the other.
But if gasoline weakness persists, it will have an increasingly bearish tug on MTBE prices, traders said.
One trader said the result of tenders from Taiwan and Thailand would be critical in signalling whether the market was weakening, or whether there was support.
The same trader said he was offering a small parcel of 2,000 tonnes of MTBE for July loading at $260 per tonne free-on-board Singapore.
Taiwan was expected to award its tender to buy August MTBE on Thursday.
Taiwan's Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) last purchased 7,000 tonnes of MTBE for July 6-20 at $270 per tonne c+f from Saudi Basic Industries Corp (SABIC).

Refiner Thai Oil Co Ltd was also seeking, by tender, up to three cargoes of 3,500 tonnes each of MTBE per month to Sri Racha to cover second-half requirements. Officials at the refinery were not available for comment.
Thailand's Bangchak Petroleum Plc was also expected to issue its next tender to buy August supplies in the next two weeks, company officials said.
In the last tender, Bangchak bought 1,500-tonnes of MTBE for delivery in the first week of July at around $260 per tonne cost-and-freight (c+f) Bangkok, from Saudi Basic Industries Corp (SABIC).
Pakistan awarded 96,000 tonnes of MTBE in a term tender covering July 1997 to June 1998 to Saudi Basic Industries Corp last week.
Traders said the term price of $3.00 over Singapore c+f quotes was slightly higher than had been expected which would offer some support.
--Singapore Newsroom (+65-870-3082)
